display_name: Attest a role's peer_inbox backlog covered through a message
description: A model-initiated attestation that advances the durable 'covered through' mark bounding peer_inbox's role-section default drain (the pull-surface boundary design). Given a role name and the arm-... message_id of the newest role message this session has processed for that role, the server looks that exact row up and stores THAT ROW's own (created_at, id) pair as the new mark — a caller can only ever name a pair that corresponds to a row that actually exists, never assert one directly. The mark is monotonic: an attestation at or below the already-stored mark is a no-op that returns the pre-existing mark unchanged, never regresses it. Once a role has a mark, peer_inbox's default drain (role_after absent, or an ordinary continuation cursor) stops returning rows at or before it; a caller that wants the pre-mark backlog echoes back the server-minted role_history_cursor peer_inbox exposes on a floor-stopped page. This verb is REGISTERED-ROUTE-ONLY: it takes no caller-supplied identity argument at all, ever. Identity is sourced exclusively from the calling bridge's own registered route (state['inference_vertex_session_id'], stamped only for a call dispatched through a registered process_call) — a one-shot solet call from the local CLI carries no such identity and is refused loud with unregistered_route. Role ownership is re-checked live at attestation time (not claim time), so a displaced prior holder cannot advance the mark past mail the new holder never saw.
embedding_description: Tell the platform 'I have read this role's mail up through message X' so the next peer_inbox call stops replaying already-seen history. Pairs with peer_inbox's role_floor_applied/role_history_cursor. Only a session that holds the role, over a registered bridge, can advance the mark — never a raw CLI call, never a caller-named timestamp.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: recipient_key (the role), covered_created_at + covered_id (the attested row's own tie-safe sort key — never a caller-asserted value), covered_message_id (the arm-... id that was attested), and attested_at (when this attestation landed). On a monotonic no-op the response carries the PRE-EXISTING mark, not the just-submitted message_id — compare covered_message_id to the request to tell a genuine advance from a no-op.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report the mark as a bound, not a receipt: 'peer_inbox's default drain for this role now stops at message_id'. Do not imply every intervening message was individually acknowledged — the mark is a single (created_at, id) boundary, not a per-message consumption record.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Call this after actually processing a role's backlog (draining role_after until next_role_cursor is null), passing the newest message_id seen — calling it early or with a stale message_id risks bounding the drain before mail was read. Do not call it speculatively to 'clear' a role you have not drained.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A WRITE with a silent-loss failure mode for the NEXT role holder if identity is wrong — the same risk class as peer_claim_role's measured instance-id-spoofing finding. No caller-supplied identity argument exists on this verb by design; every identity check below is server-sourced.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: 'name' or 'message_id' was empty. unregistered_route: the call did not arrive through a registered bridge's process_call (e.g. a one-shot solet call) — there is no server-sourced identity to attest with. state_service_unavailable: the state_service is not bound on this solet. identity_not_registered: the calling bridge's own instance id has no live peer_binding row. peer_role_not_held: the calling session does not currently hold the named role — re-check ownership (peer_holds_role) before retrying. role_message_not_found: message_id does not match any role message on record for this role — it cannot be attested because the row it would point to does not exist.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: unregistered_route: call this through a registered MCP/bridge session, never a raw solet CLI invocation. peer_role_not_held: claim the role first, or confirm you still hold it — a displaced session cannot advance another holder's mark. role_message_not_found: pass the message_id of a role message actually returned by peer_inbox for this role, not a synthesized or copied-from-elsewhere id.
